about: A fourth review found that three notes and two hints misstate a page or what a finding credits to it, and that two notes give one instruction two words. They stand as their readers wrote them, and the editor's words, which no reader of the follow-up wrote, follow each in square brackets: a correction where a note or a hint misstates a page, a note where two notes give one instruction different words. Each names the page it rests on; work/editor-corrections.json holds them and reread_numbers.py correct puts them in the reading.

items.words: of the two pages, Research Directions gives the 98.2% (against the count's 97.0%); the handoff gives the count's 97.0% and the 1.2 points the coupling adds, not 98.2% itself
items.why: The fourth review: the hint credits the coupled count's 98.2% to the handoff too, which gives only its parts.

items.words: the FluoroCap Overnight Report does say "The films-only model is the one that was deployed on 14 September"; no page says it is later than the ladder's arms, and the note's differs stands on its other ground, that the Corpus Audit gives 98.7% only for its own model's validation split, with no 8,422

items.words: the row's own 129 and 15 are the per-patient classes of Naming Vertebrae Without an Anchor (129 L4, 15 L6), the figures the finding takes from the Fluoroscopy Data Atlas's L4L6 sheet; the row differs from the finding in reading the board's counts as lateral-film counts, a scope a reader computed
items.why: The fourth review: the note gives the row's figures to the Atlas, where the row takes them from the Naming page.
